title: pam v1.0.0 — Architecture & Implementation Design
text: Transform simple R-pam package high-performance, CRAN-ready tool constructing presence-absence matrices geographic environmental space, C++17 engine via Rcpp. problem deceptively simple — convert stack species range polygons binary sites × species matrix — scale (5000+ species, millions cells, dual-space projection) demands compiled code, parallelism, sparse storage, careful algorithmic choices.

title: pam v1.0.0 — Architecture & Implementation Design
text: Bottlenecks: - terra::rasterize() single-threaded C++ (terra’s , GDAL) - Rasterizes species one call via categorical field — fast <100 species chokes 5000+ overlapping ranges - Returns dense tibble (sparse) — 5000 species × 65000 cells = 325M entries - environmental space support - coverage fraction area-weighting option - parallel processing
code: get_geo_pam(shp, res)   └─ terra::rast() → terra::rasterize() → terra::as.data.frame() → tidyr::spread()

title: pam v1.0.0 — Architecture & Implementation Design
text: use terra::rasterize? - terra rasterizes species via single categorical field — breaks overlapping ranges - Single-threaded - Returns full raster, sparse cell IDs approach: cell-centroid PIP (point--polygon) macroecological PAMs ≥0.5° resolution, centroid-based PIP test standard practice (Arita et al. 2008, 2012; letsR package). algorithm: C++ pseudocode: PIP algorithm: winding number - robust ray-casting edge cases (vertices boundary) - O(V) per point V = polygon vertices - Standard implementation Computational Geometry C (O’Rourke) Spatial index strategy: - Simple approach: per-species bounding-box filter cell centroids - large grids: lightweight R-tree cell centroids using header-implementation (Boost dependency CRAN)
code: 1. Generate grid of cell centroids for the target extent + resolution 2. For each species polygon:    a. Compute bounding box → filter candidate centroids (spatial index)    b. For each candidate centroid: ray-casting PIP test    c. Record (cell_id, species_id) pairs as sparse triplets 3. Assemble sparse matrix from triplets // Core: parallel PIP rasterization // Input:  cell_x[], cell_y[]  — centroid coordinates (n_cells) //         poly_coords[]       — packed polygon vertices per species //         species_id[]        — species index per polygon // Output: sparse triplets (cell_id, species_id)  struct Triplet { int cell; int species; };  std::vector<Triplet> pip_rasterize(     const double* cx, const double* cy, int n_cells,     const PolygonPack& polys, int n_species, int ncores) {     std::vector<std::vector<Triplet>> thread_local_results(ncores);      #pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic) num_threads(ncores)     for (int s = 0; s < n_species; ++s) {         int tid = omp_get_thread_num();         auto& bbox = polys.bbox(s);         for (int c = 0; c < n_cells; ++c) {             if (!bbox.contains(cx[c], cy[c])) continue;             if (point_in_polygon(cx[c], cy[c], polys.ring(s))) {                 thread_local_results[tid].push_back({c, s});             }         }     }     // merge thread-local vectors     return merge(thread_local_results); }

title: pam v1.0.0 — Architecture & Implementation Design
text: Algorithm: Optimal resolution E-space: Following Broennimann et al. (2012) ecospat conventions: - Default: kernel-density smoothing avoid empty-cell artifacts - discrete PAM: use Sturges’ rule Scott’s rule PC scores n_bins = ceil(1 + log2(n_points)) per axis - Provide auto_resolution() function optimizes bin count maximize information content avoiding sparsity: optimal_bins = argmin_k { KL_div(PAM_k, PAM_smooth) + λ·sparsity(k) }
code: 1. Extract bioclimatic values at cell centroids (or occurrence points)    using terra::extract() or xclim rasters 2. Run PCA on the environmental matrix (base R prcomp) 3. Define E-space grid:    - Compute range of PC1, PC2 (optionally PC3)    - Divide into n_bins per axis → n_bins² cells in E-space 4. For each species: classify occurrence points into E-space bins 5. Record (e_cell_id, species_id) presence pairs 6. Assemble E-PAM as sparse matrix

title: pam v1.0.0 — Architecture & Implementation Design
text: PAM inherently sparse (species absent cells). 5000 species × 65000 cells 1° resolution, occupancy ≈ 5-15%. Strategy: - Internal: sparse triplet vector (, j, x) C++ - Export R Matrix::dgCMatrix (compressed sparse column) - Convenience method as_tibble() backward compatibility v0.2.0 - Parquet export via arrow::write_parquet() HPC pipelines

title: pam v1.0.0 — Architecture & Implementation Design
text: Following bioclim_xt() pattern xclim: - Input: REAL() pointer aliasing R NumericMatrix — copy - Output: pre-allocate R matrix, write directly REAL() pointer - OpenMP: respect OMP_THREAD_LIMIT via pam_safe_threads() helper (copy xclim_omp.h pattern)

title: Getting Started with pam
text: pam package builds geographic presence-absence matrices (PAMs) species range polygons. PAM sites--species binary table rows grid cells columns species; cell contains 1 species range overlaps cell 0 otherwise. PAMs fundamental data structure macroecology biogeography, used computing species richness, range-diversity plots, co-occurrence analyses, input conservation-prioritisation algorithms.

title: Getting Started with pam
code: # Install from GitHub # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("alrobles/PAM")

title: Getting Started with pam
text: core workflow two steps: Load species range polygons terra::SpatVector. Call get_geo_pam() desired grid resolution. result tibble. first two columns (x, y) cell centroids; remaining columns species, coded 1/0.
code: library(pam)  # Step 1: load example data (Rodentia of Mexico) shp <- get_rodentia_mexico() shp  # Step 2: build the PAM at 1-degree resolution pam_result <- get_geo_pam(shp, res = 1) head(pam_result)

title: Getting Started with pam
text: res argument controls grid cell size units CRS (decimal degrees EPSG:4326): Higher resolution → grid cells → finer spatial detail.
code: # Fine resolution (0.5 degree ~ 55 km at the equator) pam_fine <- get_geo_pam(shp, res = 0.5) dim(pam_fine)  # Coarse resolution (2 degrees ~ 220 km) pam_coarse <- get_geo_pam(shp, res = 2) dim(pam_coarse)

title: Getting Started with pam
text: PAM, species richness per cell just row sum:
code: pam_result$richness <- rowSums(pam_result[, -(1:2)])  # Quick map with base R plot(pam_result$x, pam_result$y,      cex  = sqrt(pam_result$richness) * 0.3,      pch  = 15,      col  = hcl.colors(max(pam_result$richness))[pam_result$richness],      xlab = "Longitude",      ylab = "Latitude",      main = "Rodentia Species Richness — Mexico")

code: world_pca <- get_world_pca() terra::plot(world_pca)

title: pam: Presence-Absence Matrix Construction from Species Range Maps — pam-package
text: Constructs geographic presence-absence matrices (PAMs) species range polygons stored 'terra' SpatVector objects. Rasterizes vector geometries onto user-defined grid pivots result sites--species binary matrix suitable biodiversity analyses. Includes convenience functions retrieve example mammal range data WorldClim environmental layers projected two dimensions via Principal Component Analysis.
